recentItems.title: Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series with Simnikiwe Xabanisa and Avuyile Sawula
recentItems.description:
The Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Series is alive, and it's just getting better!

The Springboks who haven't lost back-to-back test matches in almost four years, bounced back to beat arch rivals, the All Blacks, 33-26 in the second test in Cape Town, levelling the four-match series after two games.

The four-time World Champions' victory wasn't pretty, as much as it was necessary in the context of the series and what is at stake.

As the two teams move to Johannesburg for the third test match in Soweto next weekend, we are now joined by commanding voices of the game, Simnikiwe Xabanisa and Avuyile Sawula to unpack more on the game.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | ANC on manifesto campaign trail in Orange Farm
recentItems.description:
ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa is continuing the party's manifesto campaign trail today.

Engagements are expected in Orange Farm south of Johannesburg this morning, before heading to Hammanskraal outside Pretoria this afternoon.

It's day 2 of the ANC's campaign, as the party steps up its voter engagement ahead of the elections.

SABC News political reporter, Samkele Maseko is on the ground with the latest.  

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.description:
The leadership of the South African Communist Party (SACP) gives an update on its election preparations.

SABC News reporter Zara Groenewald is covering the story for us from COSATU House in Braamfontein, Johannesburg.

recentItems.title: Feroz Khan’s hospital readmission entirely predictable: Prof Nirmala Devi Gopal
recentItems.description:
SABC News has reliably learnt that Major-General Feroz Khan of Crime Intelligence has been re-admitted into a Johannesburg hospital. 

Khan was subpoenaed to appear before the Madlanga Commission this week. He was also served with a further Rule 3 notice recently and required to answer additional questions. 

Meanwhile, reports today say that Khan has taken the SAPS to the Labour Court following a disciplinary process that could see him dismissed. 

To unpack the situation, we're joined by Professor Nirmala Devi Gopal, Professor of Criminology at UKZN.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Lesotho Princess Senate Mohato Seeiso appointed UNDP Goodwill Ambassador
recentItems.description:
Lesotho Princess, Senate Mohato Seeiso has been appointed the UNDP Lesotho National Goodwill Ambassador for Equality and Sustainable Development.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) says she stood out among a strong field of candidates, bringing the voice and influence needed to advance the development agenda.

SABC News correspondent Rapelang Radebe reports from Maseru, Lesotho. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Two friends to embark on 600 km MegaWalk to Durban in support of children with disabilities
recentItems.description:
Two friends are taking on a 600-kilometre journey on foot from Johannesburg to Durban to support children living with disabilities.

Vusumuzi Nelson Mbambani and Molelekwa Mahoko, better known as content creator MC Megacy, will undertake the MegaWalk from the first of September to the first of October, aiming to raise funds and awareness, while inspiring people living with disabilities.

Molelekwa Mahoko, famously know as MC Megacy joins us to tell us more about this initiative. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Nepal’s deadly flash floods spark new fears over global warming
recentItems.description:
Scientists are warning that a developing El Niño weather pattern could become one of the strongest in more than a century.

South Africa is bracing for a dry summer season with the El Niño peak expected to hit between October 2026 and January 2027. It's expected to bring an increased risk of heat waves and lower rainfall levels. 

Meanwhile in another developing story, devastating floods along the Nepal-China border have killed hundreds, with fears of further flooding. 

As extreme weather events become more frequent and severe, how much of this can be linked to climate change and what should we expect in the months ahead? 

To discuss this we're joined by Professor Francois Engelbrecht, Director of the Global Change Institute at Wits University.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Women's Month | Mahlatse Lekwadu on managing her business as a woman with a disability
recentItems.description:
Roughly one-third of the South African population are beneficiaries of various forms of social grants. This is according to one of the papers that was published by the University of Johannesburg. 

The Women's Report on Africa goes on further to state that these grants play an important role in ensuring that people are able to eat and obtain the most basic necessities. And a significant number of those recipients are women with disabilities.  

We shine the spotlight on the economy inclusive of women with disabilities. 

To discuss this, we are joined by Mahlatse Lekwadu, a woman living with a disability and co-founder of Magadine Business Enterprise, a company that is involved in the sphere of construction and mining supply. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.
